metadata.case_name: ABU BAKKR SHIDDIK v. ELAHI MANZOR & YAVAR ALI FORMERLY T/A MM & CO AUTO PARTS, DISMANTLING AND GENERAL (A FIRM)

injuries.description: CT brain showed fluid at sphenoid sinus
source:
CT brain showed fluid at sphenoid sinus and was managed by the
Neurosurgical Department of the Tuen Mun Hospital;
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of sphenoid bone of skull

injuries.description: macula comotio retinae of left eye (blunt trauma to left eye)
source: the plaintiff also suffered from blunt trauma to his left eye and was first seen at the Hong Kong Eye Hospital on 27 September 2007 where he was diagnosed to be suffering from macula comotio retinae with reduced VA of 1/6. The right eye was normal with normal VA of 6/5.

injuries.description: fractured 5th, 6th laminae and 7th spinal process (cervical spine fractures)

source:
CT thorax showed left haemopneumothorax with fractured ribs. Chest drain
was inserted and managed by cardiothoracic surgery of Tuen Mun Hospital;

injuries.description: bony chance fracture 11th thoracic spine; compression fracture of 12th thoracic spine and lumbar spine
injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures of lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: fracture left superior and inferior pubic rami
source:
X-ray pelvis showed fracture left superior and inferior pubic rami which
were also treated conservatively.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of pubis without disruption of pelvic ring

manifestations.description: 15% loss of central vision in his left eye which is equivalent to 3% acuity-related impairment of both eyes
residual left eye maculopathy is stable and does not require medical or surgical treatment
the plaintiff had reached Maximal Medical Improvement regarding his orthopaedic injuries
residual disability and pain which affect on a continuous basis the quality and enjoyment of his life

treatments_received.treatment: Physiotherapy and rehabilitation under Orthopaedics & Traumatology
source: The plaintiff was later transferred to the Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology on 24 September 2007 for rehabilitation under custody. Physiotherapy was offered and he was discharged on 3 October 2007 and referred back to the Tuen Mun Hospital for follow-up.

treatments_received.treatment: Ophthalmological assessment and follow-up (no medical or surgical treatment required)
source: According to the Ophthalmological report of Dr Cheung Sek Hong dated 6 September 2011, the plaintiff’s residual left eye maculopathy is stable and does not require medical or surgical treatment. Sick leave for the left eye commotion retinae should be approximately 6 weeks to 2 months.

treatments_received.treatment: Admission to Accident and Emergency and inpatient surgical ward
source: After being rescued, the plaintiff was taken to the Tuen Mun Hospital and admitted to the Accident and Emergency Department at around 14:07 hours on 27 August 2007.
Various investigations were done and he was admitted to the surgical ward for further management.

losses.description: The plaintiff suffers from a 15% loss of central vision in his left eye which is equivalent to 3% acuity-related impairment of both eyes.
residual disability and pain which affect on a continuous basis the quality and enjoyment of his life
